dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: This is an important sea route. There are tons of ships passing in and out, so I have to be vigilant in standing guard...

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: Uh... Ahaha, is it really that obvious...

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: Actually, I've always been the nervous sort. Maybe it's because I've always had sharp eyes. The more you can see, the more pressure you feel, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: I can see a long way out from here. The last time I looked out from here to the sea, I saw an outlander vessel with people on it dressed all fancy. They had masks, too.

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: ...Were they the Fatui? I have to be more careful. We can't let them reach the shore willy-nilly.

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: Yeah, I need to get back to my work as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's definitely something worth looking out for.

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: See? I knew I was right.

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: I've been more strict with people coming in and out from the harbor recently as well. We don't just need to stop Shogunate operatives from getting in, but we need to guard against smuggling and stowaways as well.

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: Harbors are transport hubs, after all. Can't ever be too careful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You should really relax a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: I've been trying, you know? I've tried all sorts of methods that a friend recommended to me, like bathing under a waterfall, jogging at midnight... and things like that.

dialogues.speaker: Nami
dialogues.text: But I don't feel like any of these measures have worked. I've asked that friend before, and he just says that I need to "bear with it for a while," and that I'll be fine once I "surpass my limits."
